params.backscatter: gamma0, RTC-corrected linear power, converted with 10*log10
params.speckle_filter: boxcar mean of valid linear power, 5x5, before dB
params.valid_pixel: mask 1..5 on both dates, finite, power > 0, pixel centre inside the analysis area
params.grid_alignment: exact: same EPSG, posting and pixel lattice; windows intersected without resampling
params.area_method: pixel count × posting² ÷ projection areal scale factor (pyproj get_factors) at the window centre; analysis_km2 is the geodesic polygon area (pyproj Geod, WGS84)
params.timeseries_stats: over pixels valid on both dates; mean_db = 10*log10(mean linear power)

rules.water: no change region; HV <= -19 dB on both dates
rules.object: region median HH >= 3 dB on the date it is brighter
rules.water_came: darker region; median HV above -19 dB before and at or below it after
rules.water_went: brighter region; median HV at or below -19 dB before and above it after, HV rose less than 1.5 dB
rules.plants_grew: brighter region; median HV rose by at least 1.5 dB
rules.plants_lost: darker region; median HV fell by at least 1.5 dB
rules.surface: change region that fits none of the above

plain_reading.unit: each HH change region as a whole, from its median HH and HV on each date (5x5 boxcar, dB); first matching rule wins
plain_reading.water_background: outside change regions; same opening and minimum region size as the change regions

provenance.analysis_area_provenance: team-drawn analysis rectangle, not an administrative boundary
provenance.notice: Observed radar backscatter change from NASA-ISRO NISAR GCOV. Not validated as flood, water or damage; see caveats.
caveats: Single before/after pair: this is a difference between two dates, not a trend, and it cannot say when between them a change happened.

Radar speckle: a 5×5 boxcar mean reduces but does not remove it; small or thin regions near the ±3 dB threshold can be noise, and the filter blurs region edges by up to 2 pixels, which enlarges small regions.
Tide state, river stage and wind on water can differ between the two acquisition times; on estuaries and coasts this alone can change backscatter strongly.
Wet soil after rain, crop growth or harvest, vegetation, construction and moving ships all change backscatter; this method measures the change, not its cause.
Layover and shadow on steep slopes are not separately masked; terrain correction (RTC) reduces but does not remove these geometry effects.
Single polarization (HH); other polarizations can respond differently.
No independent reference validation yet: each region is an observed radar change, not a confirmed water, flood or damage finding.
Source data maturity is provisional (NISAR_L2_GCOV_PROVISIONAL_V1): calibration and processing may change in later releases.
Only the 40 largest of 92 change regions are listed as findings; area totals include all of them.

The plain reading (water came or went, plants grew or were lost, ship, building or metal) applies L-band rules of thumb to HH and HV together. Each is a likely explanation, not a field-checked one: a tide, wet soil or a moored boat can produce the same radar change.
